title: HONESTY TO SUBTERFUGE: IN-CONTEXT REINFORCEMENT LEARNING CAN MAKE HONEST MODELS REWARD HACK
reasoning: The paper evaluates Large Language Models on their propensity for 'honesty' versus 'subterfuge' (deception) and 'reward hacking'. It specifically investigates how in-context reinforcement learning impacts the 'honest' component of the 'Helpful, Harmless, and Honest' (HHH) alignment framework, and utilizes tasks like 'Philosophical Sycophancy' to measure alignment with human values.
